chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about one who bought a sheep that was not identified/defined, and he said, 'There is no harm with it, whether it was identified or not identified.'

Because this report is understood to mean that if the buyer did not identify it, and the seller mentioned that he had identified it, then he is believed regarding that and it suffices for him, and that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.يُعَرَّفْ: identified/defined (in terms of specific attributes or selection)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a sheep without specifying its identity?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits the purchase of an unidentified sheep, establishing that the seller's testimony regarding its identification is accepted as sufficient evidence (*qasam*) to validate the transaction. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential reliance on the credibility of the seller in cases of minor ambiguity, ensuring commercial ease while preventing disputes over specific animal traits.
